summary:
BEYOND 30 AU:OORT ODESSEY is an interactive space-exploration concept that combines NASA’s SPHEREx infrared sky observations with AI-assisted change detection to help people investigate unusual objects and changes in the universe.

Our proposed platform, COSMOS AI, allows users to explore SPHEREx observations, compare images captured at different times and infrared bands, and identify unusual changes that may deserve further scientific investigation. Its main modules include SPHERE-VIEW for sky-image exploration, TIME-TRACK AI for highlighting possible changes, and PLANET-X RADAR for connecting candidate observations with known astronomical databases.

The project also introduces ORION-X, a conceptual future robotic spacecraft designed to investigate scientifically verified targets beyond 30 AU, including objects in the Kuiper Belt and, as a long-term exploration goal, the distant Oort Cloud.

By combining NASA data, accessible visualisation, citizen science and future-spacecraft concepts, OORT ODYSSEY aims to make planetary exploration more understandable and open to everyone.
details: 1.Introduction The universe is constantly changing, but identifying those changes across enormous astronomical datasets is a major challenge. NASA’s SPHEREx mission observes the entire sky in 102 near-infrared spectral bands and repeats its sky survey over time. These observations provide an exciting opportunity to investigate objects whose brightness, appearance or position may change. OORT ODYSSEY proposes an accessible platform called COSMOS AI to help users explore these observations and identify interesting astronomical changes. 2. How does the project work? Our proposed system has five major components: A. SPHERE-VIEW – Interactive Sky Explorer Users can explore SPHEREx observations by entering sky coordinates and selecting available observation records. They can view infrared images and compare observations from different dates. B. TIME-TRACK AI – Change Detection The system compares two observations and creates a difference image to highlight possible changes. Image-processing and AI-assisted techniques can help flag unusual regions for further examination. These are candidate signals, not confirmed discoveries. C. PLANET-X RADAR – Candidate Investigation Potentially interesting observations can be compared with known astronomical information using NASA/JPL resources such as the Small-Body Database and Horizons system. This helps users investigate whether a candidate may correspond to an already known object. D. ORION-X – Future Space Exploration Concept ORION-X is our conceptual autonomous robotic spacecraft designed for future investigation of distant Solar System targets. Its proposed scientific instruments include an imaging system, infrared spectrometer, magnetometer and dust analyser, supported by long-duration power and communication systems. E. COSMOS CITIZEN SCIENCE The platform encourages students, astronomy enthusiasts and the public to explore observations, mark unusual features and submit candidate reports for scientific review. 3. Benefits and Intended Impact Makes complex astronomical observations easier for the public to understand. Encourages citizen participation in space science. Provides a visual way to compare observations over time. Helps prioritise unusual signals for further investigation. Introduces the scientific challenges of exploring the Kuiper Belt and the distant Oort Cloud. Inspires future research into autonomous spacecraft and deep-space exploration. 4. Tools and Technologies Programming language: Python Web application: Streamlit Astronomical data access: SPHEREx IRSA SIA2 archive Data processing: NumPy and Astropy Image processing: OpenCV AI-assisted anomaly detection: Scikit-learn Visualisation: Plotly Astronomical cross-checking: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database and Horizons 5. Creativity and Innovation The uniqueness of OORT ODYSSEY is its combination of real astronomical observations, time-based image comparison, AI-assisted candidate flagging, citizen science and a future deep-space exploration concept. Instead of presenting space exploration only as a scientific topic, our project creates a pathway from observing the sky to investigating unusual signals and imagining future robotic missions. 6. Scientific Considerations SPHEREx is not specifically designed to discover Planet Nine or directly confirm planets in the Oort Cloud. Changes in astronomical images may also result from instrumental effects, image alignment or calibration differences. Therefore, our system treats unusual signals as candidates requiring independent observations, expert review and reliable orbital analysis before any scientific conclusion is made.
